items.name: XpenseSplitter
items.tagline: Shared expense tracking for group trips, with no server and no accounts.

image.alt: The XpenseSplitter landing screen, headed "Split the trip. Settle up in seconds."

items.why: Splitting costs on a trip always ends the same way: a spreadsheet nobody keeps up to date, or an app that wants everyone to make an account before it will accept a number. I wanted one where the maths is provably right and the data never leaves the people on the trip. So there is no server, no database and no sign-up — a trip is a file you can hand to someone.
features: Chronological expense ledger — amount, category, payment type, who paid, and exactly who it splits between.
Live per-person share preview while you toggle participants in and out of an expense.
Expense explorer: a read-only view to search, sort and group, so anyone can check they were included or excluded correctly.
Settlement two ways — every real pairwise debt, or the fewest transfers that clear everyone.
Autosaves locally; export or import a trip as JSON to move it between devices.
notes: Money has to land exactly. Shares use largest-remainder rounding, so a split always sums back to the total — no penny drift, and no divide-by-zero when nobody is included.

Merging a second trip is really an identity problem: the same person has a different id in each file. People are matched by name across the two, shown as plain sentences — "alice merges into Alice" — and nothing is rewritten until that mapping is confirmed.

Duplicates only become findable once identity is settled — an import matching an existing entry on amount, payer and the exact set of sharers is skipped by default. Description and date are ignored on purpose, and anything involving a newly added person is never flagged: no existing entry could have been split with someone who was not there.
Nothing is stored that can be computed. Totals, balances and settlements are all derived from the raw ledger on read, so there is never a second copy of the truth to fall out of sync with it.
